title: OPEN Forum, November 2026

cues: press 1: moves to s02 (the first picture, on the dark ground)
note.body:
[Both of you, salaam, in your own words.] We're Nadir and Sania, two of the founders of The Friends of Pakistan: a network and a fund, started this year by Pakistanis at home and abroad. We find the people already solving Pakistan's biggest problems, and help them grow to reach millions.
(press)

scenes.title: Flood relief, then food every day

cues: press 1: the right half comes into focus, Rizq's food system; the left racks out of focus and drains to black and white
press 2: moves to s03
note.body:
It's 2022. Pakistan is hit by floods of a scale we thought we'd see once in a century. Thirty-three million people affected. Eight million forced from their homes. And what happens next is extraordinary. The Edhi Foundation runs rescues. Islamic Relief brings food, clean water and shelter. When Pakistan is in need, Pakistanis show up.
[Say the left half as something you are proud this room did.]
(press)
[Must say, as the cart comes into focus: the room needs Rizq's name on this picture.]
But amid the relief, some people ask a different question. Not only how do we feed this family today, but how do we make sure this family doesn't go hungry tomorrow? Take Rizq, started by young LUMS graduates. They rescue surplus food, work with farmers, and build kitchens and food carts. Rizq says it has served more than twenty million meals.
(press)

scenes.title: A ward, then expertise brought to the family

cues: press 1: the right half comes into focus, ChildLife's telemedicine; the left racks out of focus and drains to black and white
press 2: moves to s04
note.body:
It's not only floods. A thousand children under five die in Pakistan every day, many from things a doctor could have treated. And once again, Pakistanis step up. Think of Indus Hospital, of Koohi Goth, and the doctors and nurses caring for families who couldn't otherwise pay.
[Your countdown line stays out: this session asks for no guilt. It is yours to restore.]
(press)
But again, some leaders ask a different question. What needs to change so families aren't without care in the first place? ChildLife Foundation rebuilt thirteen children's emergency rooms in public hospitals, then linked three hundred more hospitals to specialists by video. More than a million consultations. They didn't just improve a hospital. They found a way to bring expertise to the family.
(press)
note.first_line: It's not only floods.

scenes.title: A school, then the teacher in every school that stands

cues: press 1: the right half comes into focus: a teacher's hands holding a phone, a lesson lit on it; the left (a school, "Photo: The Citizens Foundation") racks out of focus and drains to black and white
press 2: moves to s05
note.body:
You could build a school. This room has built thousands of them. That is how The Citizens Foundation began: a few schools, and people like you behind them. The country needed every one.
(press)
Or you could lift what is taught in every public school, on a phone in the teacher's hands: the government schools, where most of Pakistan's children already sit. Haroon will show you what that looks like.
(press)
note.first_line: You could build a school.

scenes.title: One graduate, then every graduate ready

cues: press 1: the right half comes into focus, a career-readiness class in a public university; the left racks out of focus and drains to black and white
press 2: moves to s06
note.body:
You could help one graduate find their first job. That changes a family.
(press)
Or you could back the people teaching every public-university class how to find work. Amal Academy, one of our Skardu fellows, does exactly that. It reports that eight in ten of its sixteen thousand graduates start meaningful work within three months.
(press)
note.first_line: You could help one graduate find their first job.

press 3: moves to s10 (Sania; the ground turns to paper)

Pakistan is the seventh most generous country on earth, says this year's World Giving Report. Four times you could do one good thing, and four times the same heart could reach every family.
(press)
There is a new way of doing good.
(press)
Back what reaches millions. Sania.
(press)
note.first_line: Pakistan is the seventh most generous country on earth, says this year's World Giving Report.

cues: press 1: the axes; the steady line draws, "Steady": "the village school you sponsor"
press 2: the linear line draws, "Linear": "more schools every year"; steady recedes
press 3: the exponential curve draws, "Exponential": "how every school in Pakistan teaches"; both earlier lines recede
press 4: the chart recedes; "Exponential, not linear. A trajectory, not a number."
press 5: moves to s11
note.body:
Nadir started us off with a new way of doing good. I know scale is a buzzword, so we have one definition: the sustained acceleration towards the full potential of your idea. Scale has a shape; Kevin Starr at Mulago draws it in three lines.
(press)
The first scenario is steady impact. Think of the village whose students you sponsored. Deep, and limited in reach.
(press)
Then linear growth: more and more schools every year. Most of us call this scale. [If it is true for you: "I did too."] But the problem, I promise you, is outpacing it.
[Your original, if you want it back: "Sorry to burst the bubble here, but it's not."]
(press)
Exponential is when the solution overtakes the problem. Not one village, not a few thousand schools: how education is delivered across all of Pakistan. Now that's exciting.
(press)
It's exponential, not linear. A trajectory, not a number. All three kinds of doing good are important. Only one keeps up with the problem.
(press)
note.first_line: Nadir started us off with a new way of doing good.

scenes.title: Who delivers it, and who pays

(press)
Either the government takes it on and puts it in its budget.
(press)
Or they create a marketplace where other organisations copy the model.
(press)
Either way, the organisation's budget can level off,
(press)
even as its impact goes through the roof.
(press)
note.first_line: Organisations aiming that high know they can't do it alone.

Because when you back real scale, your dollar stretches. In our experience, for a dollar in, you get ten times the impact out.
(press)

(press)
One donor: Chuck Feeney, one man, through Atlantic Philanthropies. It gave Ireland 1.6 billion euros, most of it to its universities, and on the research it backed, the state added five dollars for each one the donor gave. None of them stopped giving to family.
(press)
note.first_line: Other communities like ours did this, on purpose.

scenes.title: The Friends of Pakistan, and the next generation

cues: press 1: "Find. Refine. Fund." fills the gap between $100 and $10 million

press 3: Taskeen; Mehfooz AI recedes in place

press 6: moves to s16
note.body:
That's why we started The Friends of Pakistan. We know how to give a hundred dollars. We know how to invest ten million. But who backs the builder whose idea already works?
(press)
We scour Pakistan for them, the next generation with the chops to scale, charities and businesses both. Find. Refine. Fund.
(press)
You might be thinking: nice try, those organisations don't exist in Pakistan. Except they do. Nadir and I have met the leaders and vetted their work. Mehfooz AI: legal help for women leaving abusive marriages. The chatbot prepares the complete court-ready file, and certified lawyers review it before filing.
(press)
Taskeen: a mental-health phone help-line that is opening up access to psychologists. Twenty-five thousand people helped.
(press)
Soby Agro: a one-stop shop for high-productivity farm products, so farmers become profitable.
(press)
Sehat Kahani: telemedicine clinics, so everyone has good healthcare within walking distance.
[Yours, if you want it (not on screen; Nadir says the number at the close): "Across our first months, we helped unlock four million dollars for three organisations." Never "these three".]
(press)
note.first_line: That's why we started The Friends of Pakistan.

note.body:
[After the Q&A. Thank Haroon and the room in your own words.] This year we trained fifteen organisations to grow, and helped unlock four million dollars for three organisations. That is our own count.
(press)
So here is your role. One slice of what you give. Back one of them, open a door for them, or join us.
(press)
Our table is just outside, all day.
(press)
Back what reaches millions. [Introduce the next speaker.]
[If asked about tax: gifts from the US go through the fiscal host named on our donate page. If asked about zakat: your own answer, as the Friends of Pakistan's policy.]
(press)
note.first_line: So here is your role.
